palette.mood: Storm slate with a muted sulphur-green key (#B9B86A), wet verdant moss slope layers, slate timber props, cool pale-grey plates (never cream, no bone, no ivory), a cool pale-grey ghost always cased in charcoal dashes or set over slate and moss, and one lantern-gold accent that appears ONLY on listening instruments, the lit side of the slope and the goat's rim at the button. Curious, honest, never alarmist.
palette.divergence: Unlike 10-31's sage-and-cream chart desk with graphite lines, 10-29's aubergine dusk depot and 10-28's green-black sonar abyss, this film is overcast daylight on a wet layered hillside, with slate timber props, grey-white plates, a standing relief map instead of a desk map, and gold reserved for listening instruments. The cream and graphite of 10-31 never appear.
palette.accent_licence: lantern-gold ONLY on: the three lit instruments and lamp cones (shot 7), the one lit lamp and the goat's lit-side rim (shot 9). Counters and coins are slate-bronze (#6E6A58), never gold, and the RainGauge is desaturated by an episode-local grade outside shot 7. SatelliteEye in shot 5 is passed lensColor, dishColor and coneColor from the feed_sat blue, never its gold defaults. SeismicStation stays at lamp 0 with emotion listening or straining outside shots 7 and 9. No gold in the Haines and Wrangell frames. The feed_shake orange is thin and low-alpha so it never reads as a second accent. The feed_ground green is the groundwater probe's line and the probe drips GREEN.
palette.ghost_render: Simulated's own colour is overridden to #EEF2F0 and its lime re-solve tick is overridden in the GhostHill wrapper. The ghost is never placed over plate grey or any light ground, only over slate or moss, and the pale break in shot 5 stays behind the real slope.

light.time: Overcast storm afternoon clearing to a warm lamp
light.direction: Flat muted sulphur-green key through rain, cool slate fill, lantern-gold rim only on lit instruments and, in shot 9, on the goat's lit side
light.depth: Three planes: foreground rain streaks and plates at z170, the slope layers and ghost at z0, slate sky and ridge at z-120. The ghost is shadowless, only the physical gauge, stations, probe, coin stacks, poles, lamps and goat take contact shadows.
light.key_note: Overcast sulphur-green key (#B9B86A, desaturated) in shots 1 to 4, thinning across shot 5 as readings arrive so the clouds visibly break by the tug beat, warm lantern-gold only where an instrument listens in shots 7 and 9.

per_shot.1: flat sulphur key, rain streaks z170, slope z0, mist ridge z-120
per_shot.2: side-lit standing relief map with real extrusion and a contact shadow under the slate-bronze coin hill, cool pale plates
per_shot.3: three panels each lit by the same overcast key, panel grounds are slate or moss never plate grey, only the real slope darkens and the ghost goes stale and frozen-grey
per_shot.4: near-black slate void, one soft top key on the RainGauge (labels off, the plate carries the number), three plain slate cards (HAINES, TWO KILLED, WRANGELL), no gold, no ghost, no lamps, rain only; any glint on the gauge is a cool neutral specular, never warm
per_shot.5: overcast thinning to a pale break, feed lines in four hues from the feed roles
per_shot.6: a hollow ghost alone on a slate void, four dead grey lines, three poles (award record, taller UW, shorter UAF) with contact shadows, a dashed test outline and an empty results plate, no slope, no ground
per_shot.7: low angle, gold rim on the three instruments only, fog smears the far side of the ghost
per_shot.8: dark cold fjord face at fjord scale, a tiny slope silhouette at its foot, ruler in cool pale-grey, no gold, no ghost
per_shot.9: low angle, one gold lamp, fog beyond, goat takes a gold rim only on the lit side

shape_language.grammar: Torn jittered slope layers and a soft round seismic station against the rectilinear plates, poles and slate cards. The ghost is the only dashed geometry, always cased in charcoal dashes or set over slate and moss, never over a light ground, drawn with a faint grid fill and fog smear so it reads as a stated model and not a plain dashed line.
shape_language.why: The story moves from organic ground to the rectilinear fair case, and the dashed ghost carries the honest word plan.

casting.net_new: Episode-local only, none registered this run: GhostHill (a wrapper over lib/simulation.tsx Simulated that adds a charcoal dashed casing under a pale-grey dashed stroke, a clipped faint grid for the planned-copy fill, two clipped Simulated instances for the sharp side (fidelity about 1) and the fog side (fidelity about 0.15) split at x 760 in shot 7, a hollow state, a stale frozen-grey state, and its own outline path data including a ghost-goat outline), the relief map, the three-panel strip, the crank machine, the four clocks, the socket post, the storm cloud, the cards, the lone pole, the results plate, the Barry Arm face, the gauge ruler. Candidates for promotion: GhostHill. Also episode-local: Lamp and Socket (replacing LampArm, whose brass and lit lens can't be overridden), a slate-bronze dial counter (replacing TallyCounter), the Fairbanks pin, green groundwater drips, a dark grade for the Barry Arm face (FjordBG is not used). RainGauge is wrapped in a desaturating grade (grayscale and dim) in shots 3, 4 and 5 so its cream wood and gold hooks never read as accent or cream, and left native only in shot 7 where gold is licensed.
casting.continuity: The Haines RainGauge from shot 4 is carried into shot 5 as the weather feed. The ghost is on screen in every act except the Haines and Wrangell hush and Barry Arm, by design.

motion_language.grammar: Rain drips settle with weight, the ghost snaps with anticipation and overshoot, the crack opens in two beats, hush frames hold with only a slow push.
hero_moves: The ghost hill snaps onto the real slope after each reading tug
The crack opens through soaked layers as the station flinches
The goat steps through fog and the ghost breaks apart under its hooves

composition.focal_hierarchy: Slope and ghost first, plates second
composition.negative_space: Hush frames for Haines and Wrangell are plain cards with large empty slate
composition.safe_area: Hero action inside y420 to 1500, captions in the open band
composition.signature_shot: Shot 7 beat id 37: from a cross-section-cutaway view the ghost is razor sharp around a RainGauge at x 200, a SeismicStation at x 400 and a ThawProbe at x 600 with the sharp-to-fog boundary at x 760, smeared to fog beyond; the ghost goat walks in sync with the real goat on the lit side then lags and dissolves in the fog.
